- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.10) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.20), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–4% to align with downward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak for next 3–5 periods.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, apply mean reversion: subtract 1–2% per period until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >5% from model, check sentiment lag: if sentiment turned positive 2–3 days prior, model may be overconfident; adjust downward.
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., +0.10 → -0.20 → +0.10), model tends to lag; forecast should be 1–2% ahead of true outcome in such cycles.
